# Plant cells: a study set

A short reading about plant cells, then a self-check.

> [!module|plant-cell-study] Plant cells

A short reading about plant cells, then a self-check.

> [!activity|pc-read repeat] Read and check

Read this first, then check yourself on the next page.

## The parts of a plant cell

- **Cell wall** — A stiff outer layer, outside the cell membrane, that gives the cell its shape and support.
- **Chloroplast** — Where photosynthesis happens: sunlight is turned into sugar, using a green pigment called chlorophyll.
- **Vacuole** — A large, water-filled sac that keeps the cell firm and stores waste and nutrients.

> [!diff] An animal cell has none of these three
> An animal cell has a membrane but no wall, no chloroplasts, and only small vacuoles if any — this is the main way the two kinds of cell differ.

Cell walls were first described from cork tissue in 1665.[^hooke-1665]

***

## Check yourself

Answer from memory first.

> [!choice|wall] What gives a plant cell its shape and support?
- [ ] The nucleus
- [x] The cell wall
- [ ] The vacuole

> [!choice|chloro] Where does photosynthesis happen in a plant cell?
- [ ] The vacuole
- [ ] The cell wall
- [x] The chloroplast

> [!text|why] Why do you think an animal cell has no cell wall?
> A guess is fine — there is no one right answer.

[^hooke-1665]: *Micrographia*, Robert Hooke (1665), p. 113: "I could exceedingly plainly perceive it to be all perforated and porous, much like a Honey-comb." Verified 2026-09-27.
